_README: Known-answer triage cases: one entry per (language, detector family) the analyzer
supports. The analyzer has no data flow analysis, so it flags the true positive and
the false positive in each pair identically. Deciding between them is the reviewer's
job, and these are the cases with a settled answer.
Verdicts live here rather than in the fixture comments so the fixtures double as eval
input: a verdict written next to the code is a verdict the reviewer reads instead of
deriving. The upstream test suite asserts the mechanical half (the analyzer
still reports both members of every pair); the verdict and rationale are for humans and
locator.kind 'function' matches Violation.function exactly; 'line-of' finds the unique
substring in the fixture and matches Violation.line, which is how the source-scan
detectors report (they attribute to '<source>', not to the enclosing function).
Our copy keeps the Rust and JavaScript fixtures only (the languages we write).

families.arith: Division, modulo or exponentiation reaching a variable-time instruction
families.branch: Conditional branch whose outcome may depend on a secret (native only, warning severity)
families.funcs: Call to a non-cryptographic RNG, reported by a source scan
families.encode: Variable-time encoding of a value that may be secret, via table lookups indexed by its bytes
families.compare: Early-exit comparison of two byte strings, where timing reveals the length of the matching prefix (warning severity)
families.lookup: Array or string index that may be derived from a secret, leaking through the cache (warning severity)

cases.why: TBNZ from the debug-build overflow check on the multiply, not a branch on any operand's value.

triage_rust.rs.notes: No branch true-positive is claimed: at O0 rustc emits no flagged conditional branch inside ct_tag_matches on arm64, so asserting one would encode a fixture artefact rather than a real detection.

cases.why: Nonce seed from Math.random() is predictable.
timing reveals the length of the matching prefix of a secret tag
the advertised algorithm identifier is public, so a prefix leak reveals nothing
index is a byte of the expanded private key, so the cache line touched depends on a secret
index is a fixed offset into a public wire header
encodes a decrypted session key, so the encoder's table is indexed by secret bytes

triage_js.js.notes: V8 compiles lazily, so this module's functions are never compiled and the bytecode detector contributes nothing; every finding here comes from the source scan.
